hive: 🐝 Good day, sir. Dabba Days is set up on your computer with nothing built yet. Nothing has been spent and there are no standing rules, so you have a clean slate and an attentive builder. What shall we build first?
We haven't met properly yet. Say "set me up" and I'll get to know your business or your product in about two minutes, or help you start something new.
🐝 Let's get you set up. First, which of these is you?
Very good. 5 quick steps, about two minutes. Say skip to any, or stop to carry on later; I keep everything as you go.

1 of 5. Your business.
What is it called, what does it do, and who are your customers? A line or two is plenty (🎙 a voice note works too).
✅ Got it, Dabba Days: Home cooks make lunch and we deliver it to office workers. We deliver Monday to Friday. Our customers are people working in offices.

2 of 5. Where it runs.
Where can I see it? Send its web address.

3 of 5. Numbers and data.
I already have the code here (15 files). So I can answer things like "how many orders this week?", send me any of these, as many as you like:
• an admin or analytics address, with its key
• a database address (please a read-only login)
• a shared spreadsheet link, or a CSV or Excel file

I only ever read; I never change your data. Keys stay on this computer. Say done when finished.

✅ dabba database: I can see 8 tables: complaints, cooks, customers, deliveries, payments, payouts, plans, subscriptions.

Anything else? Or say done.

4 of 5. How you run things.
Anything written down: policies, FAQ, price list, a pitch deck? Send the files here (PDF, text, CSV), or tell me in a few lines. Say done when finished.
📚 Read: 13 things kept, and 7 rules for how the product behaves. Anything else, or done?

5 of 5. Hosting.
Vercel, Netlify, Render, Railway, Fly or Azure? Or say don't know.

✅ All set, Dabba Days. I know 17 things about your business; read-only access to dabba database.

From now on, just tell me what you want. For example:
• "how many orders this week?"
• "show me the pricing page on desktop"
• "I want more repeat buyers"
• "add a referral page"

I'll ask only what I can't work out myself: your own rules for the unusual cases.

🐝 Sir, cooks get Rs 70 for every lunch they make, paid each Monday for the previous week. The website and your policy say the same. I checked all 161 payments in your records, and every one followed that rule and went out on a Monday. There is one thing nobody wrote down: on 12 occasions a cook was paid an extra Rs 500 marked "clean month", always on the last payout of a month, and neither your policy nor the product mentions it. Tell me what earns that bonus and I'll record it as a rule; at the moment someone is evidently adding it by hand.

hive: 🔎 Looking in your data.

steps.said: What is our refund total this month?
hive: 🔎 Looking in your data.
📊 From 1 to 14 November you refunded Rs 1,700 in cash across 12 refunds. You also gave Rs 7,600 in credits, so refunds and credits together come to Rs 9,300 over 88 deliveries.

steps.said: What was our revenue from subscriptions in October?
hive: 🔎 Looking in your data.
📊 In October you collected Rs 485800 in subscription payments from 171 payments. You also gave back Rs 4610 in refunds that month, so you kept Rs 481190 after refunds.

steps.said: Which plan is most popular among active subscribers?
hive: 🔎 Looking in your data.
📊 Veg Basic is your most popular plan, with 68 active subscribers. Veg Plus has 42 and Non-veg has 40. Paused subscribers aren't included in these numbers.

steps.said: Which area has the most active subscribers?
hive: 🔎 Looking in your data.
📊 HSR Layout has the most active subscribers, with 40, ahead of Koramangala (32), Whitefield (29) and Indiranagar (28). If you also count paused subscribers, HSR Layout is still on top with 45.

Replace the muted line with 'Fields marked optional can be left blank.' and add a price line that changes with the plan select ('Veg Basic · ₹2,400 / month for 20 lunches'), using a few lines of inline JS that read the prices 2,400 / 3,000 / 3,400.
